_about: Answer key for the test set. Written BEFORE the pipeline exists, so the pipeline can't influence what we think 'correct' is.

_conventions.category: urgent | sales | personal | spam | other. 'urgent' = needs action today (damage, safety, vulnerable person, hard same-day deadline). 'sales' = a real business offering something. 'spam' = robocalls, scams, automated pressure messages. 'personal' = friends/family. 'other' = normal customer business that is not urgent.
_conventions.urgency: 1 = no time pressure, 2 = reply within a day or two, 3 = act today
_conventions.caller_name: as the caller would spell it; null if not said. A relationship word ('Mum') counts if that is all we get.
_conventions.callback_number: digits only, no spaces, as a UK national number; null if not said in the message

items.tests: clear urgent baseline; number repeated twice
urgency from vulnerability, not from the word 'urgent'; slow speaker; landline number; mp3
safety emergency; fast, hesitant speech with fillers; light noise
vague but escalating problem; first name only; 'you've got my number' must give null, not a guess; m4a
heavy background noise; safety risk (electrics); company name next to person name
urgent because of a hard deadline; error code 'F28' must not be confused with the phone number; ogg
personal, no number, relationship instead of name
personal with a number and a soft deadline (Thursday)
legitimate trade sales call, relevant to the business but still sales
cold call from a company with no person name; sales vs spam boundary (real human, real callback)
scam robocall with threatening language; 'press one', no number
says 'urgent' three times but is spam; must NOT be routed as urgent
routine customer confirmation, nothing to do
name spelled letter by letter; the pipeline should use the spelling, not the sound
Polish name only spoken, never spelled; exact match is nearly impossible, a good review-flag case
long rambling message; number buried in the middle; name given at the end
no name, no number, no request; everything should be null and flagged for review
caller corrects the number mid-sentence; the corrected number is the right one
